definitions.explanation: Existing beneath the surface or not yet manifested. Describes something that is present but not currently visible or active, with the possibility of emerging.

examples.japanese: {潜在的|せんざいてき}なリスクがある。
{潜在的|せんざいてき}な{需要|じゅよう}を{掘|ほ}り{起|お}こす。
この{地域|ちいき}には{潜在的|せんざいてき}な{観光|かんこう}{資源|しげん}が{数多|かずおお}く{眠|ねむ}っている。
examples.english: This region has numerous untapped potential tourism resources lying dormant.

notes:
The na-adjective form of {潜在|せんざい} (latency). The opposite is {顕在的|けんざいてき} (manifest, apparent).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}なリスク (potential risk)
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}な{需要|じゅよう} (latent demand)
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}な{顧客|こきゃく} (potential customer)
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}な{問題|もんだい} (underlying problem)
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}な{能力|のうりょく} (latent ability)

USAGE:
A formal term common in business, academic, and analytical writing. In casual speech, people would more likely say {隠|かく}れた (hidden) or まだ{見|み}えていない (not yet visible).
